cd "$RUNNER_TEMP/release"
# GitHub's listing of releases can be behind a write: measured against its API on
# 2026-11-20, a draft made without files was absent from a listing made about a
# second after its creation returned and present 2.6 s after it, in three of three
# trials, while a read of the release by its id showed each write at once. So the
# look that follows this job's own write is made again while it shows what was there
# before that write: at most $looks looks, $apart seconds apart (10 and 3, so 27
# seconds at the longest).
looks=10
apart=3
version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
version="${version%-rc.*}"
files=("cairn_memory-$version-py3-none-any.whl" "cairn_memory-$version.tar.gz" SHA256SUMS)
want="$(printf '%s\n' "${files[@]}" | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' ')"
want="${want% }"
prerelease=false
candidate=()
latest=()
if [ "$CANDIDATE" = "true" ]; then
  prerelease=true
  candidate=(--prerelease --latest=false)
  latest=(-f make_latest=false)
fi
# The release's text is the version's notes and then a mark with this run's id, an
# HTML comment GitHub does not show and its API returns in the release's body. A re-run
# of the job keeps the run's id; notes.md itself is attested, so it is left as it is.
mark="<!-- cairn-ci-cd run $GITHUB_RUN_ID -->"
{ cat notes.md; printf '\n%s\n' "$mark"; } > "$RUNNER_TEMP/body.md"
# The release is made by separate requests, and nothing here takes one back. A look
# lists every release of the repository, drafts included (GitHub lists drafts to a
# token that may write, as this job's may); a listing that fails stops the job instead
# of being taken for none. The release for this tag is this run's only if it is the
# only one and carries this run's mark and this tag's pre-release flag; any other
# stops the job. (1) No release: the GitHub CLI makes one as a draft, with the files.
# Asked for a draft it publishes nothing, and its cleanup of the release it made is
# only for a draft it meant to publish itself. It sends a file again, three times at
# most, only after a failed connection or a 5xx, and removes a file only when given
# the address of one already there, which a creation never gives it. So an upload
# that fails leaves this draft, with the files that arrived, and leaves it public if
# a person published it meanwhile. (2) This run's draft, just made or left by an
# earlier attempt: its files are compared with the ones this run attested, names and
# bytes (the CLI finds a draft by its tag, as it finds a release), and a draft that does
# not hold exactly those stops the job, which says what a person does. (3) The draft
# is published by a request of its own, to the id the look gave. That is the job's
# one write to a release that exists, and it is safe: it sets draft to false and
# nothing else (for a candidate it says again, as the creation did, that it is not
# the latest), so a draft a person published meanwhile is already what it would
# make it, one a person removed makes it fail, and the files were compared first.
# When GitHub publishes and the reply is lost, the job fails and nothing is undone:
# the re-run finds the release published. (4) After each write the job looks again.
# It ends well only on a published release that holds exactly the files this run
# attested, byte for byte, which it leaves as it is: that is all a re-run does after
# an attempt that finished, so that a release tag's `aliases` runs. A look that does
# not show the job's own write is made again, as the top of this step says; when the
# last one still does not, the job stops, so it never makes a second release.
# This step's text issues no removal of a release or of a release's file and
# replaces no file.
# The mark alone does not make a release this run's: a person can change the title,
# and the notes around the mark. So each look also reads both, and the step compares
# them with what it wrote, before it publishes a draft and again on what the look
# after the publication shows; a release that differs stops the job, which then
# writes nothing more. The creation sends the title only when one is given, and the
# notes as the file holds them (cli/cli at v2.102.0,
# pkg/cmd/release/create/create.go, 453 to 458: `if opts.Name != "" {`,
# `params["name"] = opts.Name`, `if opts.Body != "" {`, `params["body"] = opts.Body`;
# 193 to 198: `b, err := cmdutil.ReadFile(notesFile, opts.IO.In)`,
# `opts.Body = string(b)`), so this step names the tag as the title itself. The title
# must be the tag, exactly, or missing or empty: an empty title is not an edited
# one. It is compared in the listing's own expression and never printed. The notes
# are compared byte for byte, and nothing
# is normalised: the listing gives them as base64, which the step decodes into a file
# and compares with the file it wrote, so no reading here drops a line end or changes
# a byte (a command substitution would drop the line ends at the end).
listing() {
  gh api --paginate "repos/$GH_REPO/releases?per_page=100" \
    --jq ".[] | select(.tag_name == \"$GITHUB_REF_NAME\") | [.id, .draft, .prerelease, ((.body // \"\") | contains(\"$mark\")), (.name | . == null or . == \"\" or . == \"$GITHUB_REF_NAME\"), ((.body // \"\") | @base64), ([.assets[].name] | sort | join(\" \"))] | @tsv"
}
unlisted() {
  echo "::error::the repository's releases could not be listed, so whether $GITHUB_REF_NAME has one is not known; re-run this job"
  exit 1
}
refuse() {
  echo "::error::a GitHub release for $GITHUB_REF_NAME exists and is not one this run can finish: $1; look at it on the repository's releases page, delete it if nobody should publish it, and re-run this job"
  exit 1
}
unfinished() {
  echo "::error::the GitHub release for $GITHUB_REF_NAME is a draft that an earlier attempt of run $GITHUB_RUN_ID left unfinished, which this job neither deletes nor publishes; delete it on the repository's releases page and re-run this job, which makes the release again"
  exit 1
}
unread() {
  echo "::error::the files of the GitHub release for $GITHUB_REF_NAME, $state, could not be downloaded, so they were not compared and nothing shows that they differ; re-run this job, and delete nothing"
  exit 1
}
differs() {
  echo "::error::the GitHub release for $GITHUB_REF_NAME, $state, carries run $GITHUB_RUN_ID's mark and differs from what that run wrote in its $1; delete it on the repository's releases page if it is still a draft, or put back what the run wrote, and re-run this job"
  exit 1
}
# What GitHub lists for the tag now: nothing (found is empty), or this run's release.
# The notes are the sixth field, empty only when the release has no text, and then
# it has no mark and the job has stopped before it reads further.
look() {
  found="$(listing)" || unlisted
  [ -n "$found" ] || return 0
  count="$(printf '%s\n' "$found" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
  [ "$count" = 1 ] || refuse "there are $count releases for it"
  IFS=$'\t' read -r id draft pre ours titled notes names <<< "$found"
  [ "$ours" = true ] || refuse "its text does not carry run $GITHUB_RUN_ID's mark"
  [ "$pre" = "$prerelease" ] || refuse "its pre-release flag is $pre, not $prerelease"
  state=public
  [ "$draft" = false ] || state="a draft"
}
# Whether the names listed are some of this run's three files, not all, and no other.
some_files() {
  local name left=" $want " listed=()
  [ "$names" != "$want" ] || return 1
  IFS=' ' read -r -a listed <<< "$names"
  for name in "${listed[@]}"; do
    case "$left" in
      *" $name "*) left="${left/ $name / }" ;;
      *) return 1 ;;
    esac
  done
}
# The look after this job's own write, made again, $looks times at most, while the
# listing still shows what was there before it: no release after the creation ($1
# is made), this run's release still a draft after the publication (published).
# After the creation it also waits while the listing shows this run's draft with
# some, not all, of its three file names and no other, since the uploads take about
# as long as the listing is behind; then the files are compared as before.
# Nothing else is waited for: any other state stops the job inside look, at once,
# and no release after the publication is none of the two.
look_after() {
  local n=1
  look
  while [ "$n" -lt "$looks" ]; do
    if [ "$1" = made ]; then
      [ -z "$found" ] || { [ "$draft" = true ] && some_files; } || break
    else
      { [ -n "$found" ] && [ "$draft" = true ]; } || break
    fi
    sleep "$apart"
    n=$((n + 1))
    look
  done
}
# Its title against the tag, and its notes against the text this run wrote.
same_text() {
  local what=""
  [ "$titled" = true ] || what=title
  printf '%s' "$notes" | base64 --decode > "$RUNNER_TEMP/listed.md"
  cmp -s "$RUNNER_TEMP/body.md" "$RUNNER_TEMP/listed.md" || what="${what:+$what and }notes"
  [ -z "$what" ] || differs "$what"
}
# Its files against the ones this run attested: the names listed, then the names and
# the bytes downloaded into $2. $1 is what a difference does. A download that fails
# is not a difference: the job stops and says so, and a re-run compares again.
same_files() {
  [ "$names" = "$want" ] || "$1" "its files are [$names], not [$want]"
  gh release download "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/$2" || unread
  names="$(ls -A "$RUNNER_TEMP/$2" | LC_ALL=C sort | tr '\n' ' ')"
  [ "${names% }" = "$want" ] || "$1" "its files are [${names% }], not [$want]"
  for name in "${files[@]}"; do
    cmp -s "$name" "$RUNNER_TEMP/$2/$name" || "$1" "$name is not the file this run attested"
  done
}
look
if [ -z "$found" ]; then
  gh release create "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" --draft --verify-tag --title "$GITHUB_REF_NAME" \
    --notes-file "$RUNNER_TEMP/body.md" "${candidate[@]}" "${files[@]}"
  look_after made
fi
if [ -n "$found" ] && [ "$draft" = true ]; then
  same_text
  same_files unfinished draft
  gh api --method PATCH "repos/$GH_REPO/releases/$id" --silent -F draft=false "${latest[@]}"
  look_after published
fi
if [ -z "$found" ] || [ "$draft" = true ]; then
  echo "::error::GitHub does not list the release for $GITHUB_REF_NAME as this job has just left it; re-run this job, which starts from what is listed then"
  exit 1
fi
same_text
same_files refuse published
echo "The GitHub release $GITHUB_REF_NAME is this run's and is published, with the title and the notes this run wrote and exactly the files this run attested."
